I am an old woman here in Mtwara, and my small piece of land is all I have. I never went to school, so I do what my mother did and what I see my neighbors doing — cassava and maize together on the same plot, because if the rains fail the cassava will still feed me. I have no money for the fertilizer from the shop, and one bag is too much for my little plot anyway; I just save the seed from last harvest and plant it again with a few beans between the rows. I put the goat droppings and the ash from my cooking fire on the plot when I can, and I weed with my own hands because there is no money to pay anyone.
